title: Qualitätsmanager (m/w/d) - Lieferantenqualität & Produktprüfung
description:
Es ist Feierabend und du verlässt das Office, happy und mit einem starken Gefühl. Dein erster Tag bei PRESCH war einfach stark 🔥

Du hast dir das Sortiment angesehen: über 500 aktive Artikel, vom Hammer bis zum Säbelsägeblatt, Lieferanten über halb Asien verteilt, Verkauf in mehr als zwanzig Länder. Und du hast sofort gesehen, wo das System noch fehlt. Nicht weil hier niemand hinschaut — sondern weil bisher niemand die Aufgabe hatte, aus einzelnen Prüfungen eine Systematik zu machen.

Genau das wird deine Aufgabe. Wir erweitern unsere Qualitätssicherung deutlich, weil wir immer mehr eigene Produkte entwickeln. Du bekommst keine fertige Struktur vorgesetzt, du entwirfst sie 💪

Und du merkst schnell: Hier wird nicht geredet, hier wird gemacht. Kurze Wege, direkter Draht zur Geschäftsführung, Entscheidungen am selben Tag.

Aufgaben

🛠️ Du gibst frei — oder eben nicht. Vor jeder Verschiffung kommt ein Muster aus der laufenden Produktion zu dir. Du prüfst nach Maß, Werkstoff, Oberfläche und Funktion, dokumentierst das Ergebnis im Erstmusterprüfbericht und entscheidest, ob die Ware rausgeht. Ohne dein Ja bewegt sich nichts.

🛠️ Du baust die Prüfsystematik auf. Prüfvorschriften je Warengruppe und je Artikel, Stichprobenumfang und Annahmezahlen nach AQL, Freigabemuster als verbindlicher Vergleichsmaßstab, Rückverfolgbarkeit von jedem Befund zu Charge und Lieferant. Reproduzierbarkeit ist der Anspruch: Dieselbe Prüfung muss in zwei Jahren dasselbe Ergebnis liefern.

🛠️ Du prüfst nach, was tatsächlich angekommen ist. Wenn die Charge im Lager eintrifft, kommt ein Muster daraus zu dir und wird gegen das verwahrte Freigabemuster abgeglichen. Genau hier fallen die Fälle auf, in denen etwas anderes geliefert wurde als freigegeben. Denn nicht nur die erste Lieferung muss stimmen, sondern die zwanzigste auch.

🛠️ Du prüfst über das gesamte Sortiment. Handwerkzeug vom Hammer über Schraubendreher, Zangen und Schlüssel bis zu Messwerkzeug und Schutzausrüstung. Und Elektrowerkzeug-Zubehör: Bohrer, Bits, Säbelsägen-, Stichsägen- und Kreissägeblätter, Schleifmittel. Handwerkzeug beurteilst du statisch, Zubehör nur unter Last — mit definiertem Prüfwerkstoff und Abbruchkriterium, damit Standzeiten vergleichbar bleiben.

🛠️ Du machst Qualität messbar. Fehlerquoten je Lieferant, Warengruppe und Charge, Reklamations- und Rückläuferquoten je Artikel, qualitätsbezogene Lieferantenbewertung. Damit im Einkauf mit Zahlen entschieden wird und nicht mit Eindrücken.

🛠️ Du gehst Kundenfehlern auf den Grund. Reklamationen, Rückläufer und Produktbewertungen sind die schnellste Qualitätsmeldung, die wir bekommen — schneller als jeder Lieferantenbericht. Du liest sie als Befund, ordnest sie der Charge zu und schließst den Kreis zum Lieferanten.

🛠️ Du steuerst unsere externen Prüfinstitute. Wo eine Norm eine akkreditierte Prüfung verlangt — VPA, TÜV, VDE — holst du Angebote, beauftragst, verfolgst Termine und bewertest die Berichte. Du behältst den Überblick, welche Norm für welche Warengruppe gilt.

🛠️ Du richtest unsere Prüfwerkstatt ein. Prüfplätze, Messmittel, Prüfwerkstoffe, Prüfmittelverwaltung mit Kalibrierintervallen. Du entscheidest mit, mit welchem Equipment du arbeitest.

🛠️ Du arbeitest mit unserem QC-Officer in Asien zusammen. Er prüft vor Ort in den Werken, du bewertest seine Berichte und gibst die Prüfanforderungen vor. Zwei Kontrollpunkte, ein System.

Dein Impact nach 12 Monaten

🛠️ Es gibt eine Prüfsystematik, nach der auch jemand anderes prüfen könnte — mit Prüfvorschriften, AQL-Niveaus und Freigabemustern für die wichtigsten Warengruppen.

🛠️ Keine Sendung verlässt die Produktion ohne dokumentierte Freigabe. Und die Prüfung ist trotzdem kein Nadelöhr.

🛠️ Jeder Befund ist zu Charge, Lieferant und Produktionszeitraum zurückverfolgbar.

🛠️ Es gibt ein monatliches Qualitätsreporting, das im Einkauf tatsächlich benutzt wird.

🛠️ Reklamationen und Rückläufer sind messbar zurückgegangen, weil Fehler bei dir auffallen und nicht beim Kunden.

🛠️ Die Prüfwerkstatt steht, inklusive Verschleißprüfung unter Last.

Qualifikation

🛠️ Technische Ausbildung mit Weiterbildung zum Techniker oder Meister, oder ein technisches Studium. Maschinenbau, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen, Qualitätsmanagement oder vergleichbar — die Richtung ist offener als du denkst, die Praxis zählt mehr als der Abschluss.

🛠️ Zwei bis fünf Jahre in Qualitätssicherung oder Qualitätsmanagement. Idealerweise in einem Unternehmen, das beschafft statt selbst fertigt, mit internationalen Lieferanten.

🛠️ Erstbemusterung, Prüfplanung und AQL sind für dich keine Abkürzungen, sondern Alltag. Du hast schon Erstmusterprüfberichte geschrieben und Annahmezahlen festgelegt.

🛠️ Du verstehst Werkzeug als Anwender. Du hast selbst gebohrt, gesägt und geschraubt und weißt, wie sich ein gutes Werkzeug anfühlt. Ohne das bleibt jede Beurteilung eine Zahl ohne Bedeutung.

🛠️ Reproduzierbarkeit ist dein Anspruch, nicht deine Pflicht. Du hältst fest, was du feststellst — Messwert, Bild, Bedingung, Urteil. Weil ein Befund nur dann etwas wert ist, wenn er sich in zwei Jahren noch nachvollziehen lässt.

🛠️ Du bleibst standfest. Eine Sperrung hält Ware auf, und dann wird es unbequem. Wer im Zweifel freigibt, um Ruhe zu haben, macht in dieser Rolle den teuersten Fehler.

🛠️ KI ist dein tägliches Werkzeug. Wir arbeiten damit im ganzen Unternehmen. Wenn du damit schon Auswertungen, Vorlagen oder Abläufe gebaut hast, passt du gut zu uns.

🛠️ Sehr gutes Deutsch und gutes Englisch. Du sprichst direkt mit unseren Herstellern und liest Prüfberichte im Original.

Bonus: Erfahrung mit asiatischen Lieferanten. Erfahrung mit Messmitteln wie Messschieber, Härteprüfung oder Drehmomentprüfung. Kenntnis der Normen für Werkzeug und Elektrowerkzeug-Zubehör. Erfahrung mit Verschleiß- und Standzeitprüfungen. Erfahrung im Aufbau eines QM-Systems oder einer Prüfstelle. Und wenn du eine Prüfvorschrift oder ein Prüfkonzept mitbringst, das du selbst geschrieben hast — zeig es uns. Wir wollen sehen, wie du denkst, nicht nur was im CV steht.

Benefits

🛠️ Du baust die Funktion auf, nicht nur den Prüfplatz. Prüfsystematik, Kennzahlen, Lieferantenbewertung, Prüfwerkstatt — du entscheidest, wie Qualität bei PRESCH funktioniert. Bei weiterem Wachstum wird daraus ein eigener Bereich mit Team.

🛠️ Direkter Draht zur Geschäftsführung. Kein Konzern-Reporting, keine Zwischenebene. Du berichtest direkt und bekommst Entscheidungen am selben Tag.

🛠️ Deine Freigabe hat Gewicht. Ohne dein Ja geht keine Ware raus. Das ist Verantwortung, die man nicht in jeder Qualitätsstelle bekommt.

🛠️ Gleitzeit. Du willst Job und Familie die gleiche Zeit widmen und sehnst dich daher nach einem flexiblen Arbeitszeitmodell? Kein Problem! Wir integrieren die Arbeit in unser Leben und nicht andersherum.

🛠️ Homeoffice-Tage für die Schreibtischanteile deiner Arbeit — Auswertungen, Prüfvorschriften, Reporting. Geprüft wird vor Ort, alles andere in Absprache mit dem Team.

🛠️ Du willst dich weiterentwickeln — Qualitätsmanagement, Messtechnik, Normenwissen, Auditorenqualifikation? Alles klar, dann los! Wir legen großen Wert auf deine Weiterbildung und schaffen den finanziellen und zeitlichen Rahmen dafür.

🛠️ Betriebliche Altersvorsorge mit unserem Zuschuss.

🛠️ 30 Tage Urlaub.

🛠️ Mitarbeiterrabatt auf unser komplettes Werkzeugsortiment.

🛠️ Unsere Hierarchien sind flach, der Zusammenhalt ist groß: Wir feiern unseren Erfolg. Wissensaustausch, Glühweinabende, BBQ und regelmäßige Teamevents erwarten dich bei uns. Getränke sind selbstverständlich dabei.

🛠️ Du bist in alle Geschehnisse unseres jungen und wachsenden Unternehmens einbezogen und führst deine eigenen Projekte.

Wenn du Qualitätssicherung nicht verwalten, sondern aufbauen willst — dann freuen wir uns auf dich!

title: Senior Avionics System Engineer
description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.

We are looking for an Avionics Systems Engineer to support the design, development, integration, and validation of spacecraft avionics systems. The role focuses on delivering robust and reliable electronic systems for data handling, communications, and control across all mission phases.

The engineer will contribute to system architecture definition, interface management, verification activities, and requirements engineering, while working closely with multidisciplinary teams and external stakeholders. In this role, you might be assigned to different avionics systems of the spacecraft.

Key Responsibilities

System Design & Architecture

  • Define and develop avionics system architectures, including electronics, data handling, and communication functions.

  • Ensure end-to-end consistency of data flows, interfaces, and system-level requirements.

  • Support selection and definition of avionics equipment, computing platforms, sensors, and communication hardware.

  • Contribute to spacecraft-level trade-offs between performance, reliability, mass, power, and cost.

Communications & Data Handling

  • Define onboard and ground-related communication and data handling concepts.

  • Support implementation of telemetry, telecommand, and data distribution architectures.

  • Ensure reliable data acquisition, processing, storage, and transmission under mission constraints.

  • Contribute to bandwidth, timing, and data budget analyses.

Integration & Interface Management

  • Define and manage interfaces between avionics and other spacecraft subsystems (power, propulsion, GNC, payload, etc.).

  • Ensure compatibility between spacecraft, launch vehicle, and ground segment interfaces.

  • Coordinate interface definitions with internal teams, suppliers, and external stakeholders.

External Regulatory & Certification Leadership

Strong ability to technically present, defend, and substantiate avionics subsystem designs and verification evidence with external regulatory and certification authorities, including NASA, ESA, and other government agencies, supporting spacecraft qualification, safety, and flight certification.

Verification & Validation

  • Define and support verification and validation strategies for avionics systems.

  • Participate in simulation, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL), and system-level testing activities.

  • Analyze test results, identify anomalies, and drive corrective actions.

  • Ensure compliance with system performance and reliability requirements.

Requirements Engineering

  • Capture, analyze, and manage system and subsystem requirements.

  • Ensure full traceability from mission objectives to implementation and validation.

  • Contribute to system documentation, including specifications, interface control documents, and test plans.

  • Ensure compliance with applicable space standards and engineering best practices.

Cross-functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with software, hardware, systems, operations, and mission engineering teams.

  • Participate in design reviews, technical exchanges, and system trade-off discussions.

  • Support alignment with external partners, suppliers, and customers.

  • Contribute to integration campaigns, launch preparation, and mission operations support.

Required Qualifications

  • Degree in Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, or equivalent.

  • +7 years experience in avionics systems, electronics, embedded systems, or spacecraft engineering.

  • Strong understanding of:

    • Electronic and embedded system architectures

    • Communication and data handling principles

    • System integration and interface management

  • Experience with requirements engineering and system lifecycle development.

  • Knowledge of verification and validation methods, including testing and simulation.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to work in multidisciplinary engineering environments.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in spacecraft avionics or aerospace systems.

  • Familiarity with space communication and data standards (e.g., CCSDS).

  • Experience with HIL testing, simulation environments, or digital engineering tools.

  • Exposure to safety-critical or mission-critical system development.

  • Experience working in international or multi-stakeholder engineering teams.

description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.

We are looking for an Avionics Systems Engineer to support the design, development, integration, and validation of spacecraft avionics systems. The role focuses on delivering robust and reliable electronic systems for data handling, communications, and control across all mission phases.

The engineer will contribute to system architecture definition, interface management, verification activities, and requirements engineering, while working closely with multidisciplinary teams and external stakeholders. In this role, you might be assigned to different avionics systems of the spacecraft.

Key Responsibilities

System Design & Architecture

  • Define and develop avionics system architectures, including electronics, data handling, and communication functions.

  • Ensure end-to-end consistency of data flows, interfaces, and system-level requirements.

  • Support selection and definition of avionics equipment, computing platforms, sensors, and communication hardware.

  • Contribute to spacecraft-level trade-offs between performance, reliability, mass, power, and cost.

Communications & Data Handling

  • Define onboard and ground-related communication and data handling concepts.

  • Support implementation of telemetry, telecommand, and data distribution architectures.

  • Ensure reliable data acquisition, processing, storage, and transmission under mission constraints.

  • Contribute to bandwidth, timing, and data budget analyses.

Integration & Interface Management

  • Define and manage interfaces between avionics and other spacecraft subsystems (power, propulsion, GNC, payload, etc.).

  • Ensure compatibility between spacecraft, launch vehicle, and ground segment interfaces.

  • Coordinate interface definitions with internal teams, suppliers, and external stakeholders.

External Regulatory & Certification Leadership

Strong ability to technically present, defend, and substantiate avionics subsystem designs and verification evidence with external regulatory and certification authorities, including NASA, ESA, and other government agencies, supporting spacecraft qualification, safety, and flight certification.

Verification & Validation

  • Define and support verification and validation strategies for avionics systems.

  • Participate in simulation, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL), and system-level testing activities.

  • Analyze test results, identify anomalies, and drive corrective actions.

  • Ensure compliance with system performance and reliability requirements.

Requirements Engineering

  • Capture, analyze, and manage system and subsystem requirements.

  • Ensure full traceability from mission objectives to implementation and validation.

  • Contribute to system documentation, including specifications, interface control documents, and test plans.

  • Ensure compliance with applicable space standards and engineering best practices.

Cross-functional Collaboration

  • Work closely with software, hardware, systems, operations, and mission engineering teams.

  • Participate in design reviews, technical exchanges, and system trade-off discussions.

  • Support alignment with external partners, suppliers, and customers.

  • Contribute to integration campaigns, launch preparation, and mission operations support.

Required Qualifications

  • Degree in Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, or equivalent.

  • +3 years experience in avionics systems, electronics, embedded systems, or spacecraft engineering.

  • Strong understanding of:

    • Electronic and embedded system architectures

    • Communication and data handling principles

    • System integration and interface management

  • Experience with requirements engineering and system lifecycle development.

  • Knowledge of verification and validation methods, including testing and simulation.

  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to work in multidisciplinary engineering environments.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in spacecraft avionics or aerospace systems.

  • Familiarity with space communication and data standards (e.g., CCSDS).

  • Experience with HIL testing, simulation environments, or digital engineering tools.

  • Exposure to safety-critical or mission-critical system development.

  • Experience working in international or multi-stakeholder engineering teams.

Why you should join us!

What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:  

  • We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind 

  • We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them  

  • We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. It’s a wonderful and rare opportunity, are YOU up for the challenge?  

We'd love to hear from you if you wish to be a part of our journey. Please submit your CV now for immediate consideration and we will be in touch shortly. 
 
The Exploration Company is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status or disability status. Relocation assistance is provided for those willing to relocate including visa sponsorship where applicable.  


All offers are contingent upon the successful completion of a background check, which will be subject to the country, role, and project you applied for. By submitting your application, you acknowledge and agree that any offer of employment may be conditional upon successful condition of this check. The Exploration Company partners with Zinc Work Limited located in the UK (Zinc), a third-party provider, to ensure this process as efficient and transparent as possible.

If applicable, you will receive an email from Zinc upon acceptance of your offer with a link to a secure portal where you can provide the required information to Zinc.

title: Deployment Strategist
description:
About Atira

Atira builds the commercial brain for industrials. Our agents 10x the sales engineers of today by offering the complete toolbox of tasks needed in complex environments. They handle everything from extracting and classifying requirements from incoming RFQs, orchestrating communication and information retrieval across multiple stakeholders and systems, while generating outcomes like documentation, production system inputs, or configuration recommendations. CRM. Atira. ERP.

We are one of the fastest growing teams in Munich and are looking for you to join us!

Why Deployment Strategists are our customers' #1 go-to person

We aim to solve the most complex problems in sales engineering and work closely with customers in mapping out their ideal inbound process. You will dive into our enterprise customers processes to help deploy Atira agents with our FDEs and face their most intricate challenges. You are the go-to person inside our largest partners for anything project management and use case scoping related, and this from the point where you demo our product for the first time up until multi-annual partnership commercial negotiations.
Trust and use case insights are your two most valuable resources you get from customers and what you bring back home will directly shape our core platform in the near future - this requires a strong taste when it comes to how a software product is shaped and a strong opinion on what is needed to maximize customer satisfaction. Beyond that, our Deployment Strategists think beyond a single customer and are essential in figuring out the concrete steps to scale to our next 100 customers by accelerating onboarding processes and increasing customer satisfaction.

What you will do

  • Own the customer end-to-end together with an FDE Tech Lead. From kickoff to renewal, you are on the hook. You run SteerCos, scope deployments, drive onboarding, and decide what gets built next.

  • Scope the agents that work best for a customer You go deep on each customer's technical sales process, understanding it in all it’s details. You bring home whatever solves their problems and conceptualize this across all of your customers

  • Decide what scales and what doesn't. You sit at the boundary between customer work and the core platform. You translate customer behavior into product feedback features and will need to be opinionated on product / our agents

  • Identify, elevate and partner with end users as well as C-Level. You support the internal owner and help scope the long term growth plan.

  • Tell the story. You speak at industry events, co-author case studies, and represent Atira in front of customer executives and prospects. The GTM motion is built around the stories you create

What we are looking for

Ownership, drive, structured thinking, and the ability to thrive in ambiguity and open ended problems. You take problems personally, decide in the absence of a clear roadmap, and own the outcome including the downside.

Your profile

  • Demonstrated ownership and initiative: a company you started, a leading role in a team or larger project

  • 3+ Years customer facing experience working with both end users and C-Level

  • You thrive in customer-facing situations: high-stakes conversations with executives energize you, you push back when needed, and you walk out with a clear next step

  • You’ve optimized your AI tooling: you’ve invested heavily in building the skills and context layer to get the maximum out of your day

  • Relevant coding or strong analytical experience

  • Full working proficiency in both German and English

  • Frontend and app-building / Feature taste

  • Occasional on-site travel per customer requirements; 20-40% overall (DACH primarily, occasionally international)

What you'll get

  • Real ownership: you'll be one of the early team members and shape both product and comapny as well as work closely with customers

  • Strong peers: work with people who have built and shipped AI systems in industrial environments at scale before, and the chance to learn directly from them

  • Impactful work: your code is deployed all across Europe’s and US industrial backbone, affecting how complex products and services are sold and configured worldwide

  • Competitive salary & equity package and additional benefits including Wellpass, JobRad and company dinners

  • Most importantly: Collaborate & thrive in a high-performing but caring culture. We will own the industrial sales function but will do so with modesty and integrity

What success looks like after a few months

  • You independently run enterprise deployments end-to-end, from kickoff to production

  • Customers rely on you as their primary contact and trust your judgment

  • Your learnings have shaped core platform features and the playbook for the customers who come after you

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
About Nucs AI

Nucs AI is revolutionizing prostate cancer care through cutting-edge AI and medical imaging technology. Founded in 2024 by a multidisciplinary team of oncologists, AI researchers, and healthcare innovators, we're tackling one of medicine's most pressing challenges: the growing demand for accurate, timely cancer diagnostics in the face of rising scan volumes and limited radiologist capacity.

Our mission is to enhance diagnostic precision and expand access to expert-level prostate cancer screening, ultimately improving patient outcomes worldwide.

The Opportunity

Join our engineering team as a Full Stack Engineer and help build the next generation of medical imaging platforms. You'll work at the intersection of healthcare and technology, developing secure, scalable systems that directly impact patient care and clinical workflows.

You'll design and implement robust distributed systems that power our AI diagnostic tools—architecting services that handle sensitive medical data reliably, scale gracefully under load, and integrate seamlessly with hospital infrastructure.

What You'll Build

  • Scalable microservices architectures using Kubernetes for orchestration and deployment

  • Event-driven systems with RabbitMQ for reliable asynchronous processing of medical data

  • Robust FastAPI backends that process and serve medical imaging data at scale

  • Production-grade CI/CD pipelines with comprehensive testing, monitoring, and rollback capabilities

  • Scalable data architectures using SQL databases with smart indexing and caching strategies

  • Monitoring, logging, and alerting systems that ensure reliability in clinical environments

  • Seamless integrations between internal services and external healthcare systems (HL7, FHIR)

  • Modern React frontends for clinical workflows and data management

What You Bring

  • 3+ years of full-stack engineering experience with shipped products that real users depend on

  • Strong system design skills with experience architecting distributed systems and microservices

  • DevOps expertise with Kubernetes, containerization, CI/CD, and Google Cloud Platform

  • Backend proficiency in Python with Flask or FastAPI for building reliable APIs and services

  • Database expertise in SQL and relational data modeling for handling complex medical data

  • Experience with message queues and event-driven architecture patterns

  • Clear communication skills and a pragmatic approach to solving complex technical problems

  • Frontend competency in TypeScript and React

Bonus Points

  • Experience in healthcare/medical software development

  • Knowledge of regulatory requirements (GDPR, ISO 13485)

  • Experience integrating ML/analytics into production workflows

  • Strong security mindset with experience in threat modeling and compliance

  • Familiarity with infrastructure-as-code tools (Terraform, Pulumi)

  • Experience with WebGL, WebGPU, or medical imaging frameworks (Cornerstone3D, VTK.js)

Why This Role Matters

Your work will directly contribute to advancing cancer care technology. Every system you build, every optimization you make, and every integration you design helps medical professionals provide better care to patients facing one of life's most challenging diagnoses.

Interview Process

Phone Screening (10 minutes) - Brief discussion of your key work highlights and career achievements.

Technical Interview - You'll work through technical challenge(s), presenting solutions while explaining your problem-solving approach and reasoning.

Cultural Interview - Discuss team fit and ask questions about the role and company culture.

title: Account Executive (m/w/d) Legal Tech – DACH
description:
Where Legal Leads. 

Drei Worte. Eine Überzeugung. Rechtsabteilungen sind nicht länger die Bremse im Unternehmen – sie sind der Hebel. Bei DiliTrust geben wir ihnen die Plattform, die diesem Anspruch gerecht wird: Verträge, Beteiligungen, Vorstandsarbeit und Legal AI – eine integrierte Suite für die gesamte Rechtsfunktion. Im Einsatz bei mehr als 3.000 Unternehmen in 64 Ländern, darunter führende Konzerne in Europa, Nordamerika und MEA. 

DACH ist unser nächster großer Wachstumsmarkt. Die Basis steht, jetzt skalieren wir. Du übernimmst ein eigenes Territory, baust deine Strategie eigenständig auf und entscheidest, wo du wachsen willst – unterstützt von einem Team aus Solution Consultants, BDR, Marketing und Customer Success, das in DACH bereits liefert. 

Der Legal-Tech-Markt ist über 16 Milliarden Dollar schwer und wächst jedes Jahr zweistellig. In zwei Jahren wirst du auf diesen Moment zurückblicken. 

Die Frage ist nur: Warst du dabei? 


Deine Rolle 
 

Du verantwortest ein eigenes Vertical in DACH, z.B. Financial Services, Energy, Manufacturing oder Pharma. Dein Fokus liegt auf Neukundengewinnung und gezieltem Cross-Sell in deinem bestehenden Portfolio. 

  • Du identifizierst und qualifizierst neue Opportunities, gemeinsam mit deinem BDR, über Anfragen, Marketing und gezielte Ansprache. 

  • Du arbeitest strukturiert, nicht aus dem Bauch. Du baust deinen Territory Plan auf, entwickelst Account Plans für deine Top-Targets und treibst gemeinsam mit deinem BDR fokussierte Pod Sprints in deinem Vertical. 

  • Deine Deals liegen typischerweise zwischen 50.000 € und 200.000 € Jahresvolumen. Sales-Cycles dauern 4–9 Monate. Pro Deal sprichst du mit 4–7 Entscheidern: Legal, IT, Einkauf, Finance, manchmal Vorstand. 

  • Du verkaufst eine Plattform, kein Einzelprodukt. Erstgespräche führen oft Legal Ops Manager oder General Counsel. Deals über mehrere Module sind bei uns die Regel. 

  • Du repräsentierst DiliTrust auf den wichtigen Branchen-Events wie z.B. Legal Revolution oder LegalTech. Du führst dort die Gespräche, die später zu Pipeline werden. 


Must-have

  • 4+ Jahre Erfahrung im quotaverantwortlichen B2B-Software-Vertrieb, idealerweise im SaaS-Umfeld. 

  • Erfahrung in komplexen Sales-Cycles mit mehreren Entscheidern aus Legal, IT, Finance oder Procurement. 

  • Methodisches Arbeiten: Du qualifizierst sauber (z. B. mit MEDDPICC) und führst belastbare Forecasts. 

  • Erfahrung im Verkauf an C-Level-Entscheider. 

  • Deutsch auf Muttersprachen-Niveau, sehr gutes Englisch – unsere Unternehmenssprache ist Englisch. 


Nice-to-have

  • Erfahrung im Verkauf an Rechts-, Governance- oder Compliance-Funktionen. 

  • Du kennst die Welt regulierter Branchen - Financial Services, Energy, Healthcare oder Pharma. 

  • Du hast bereits eigenständig ein Territory aufgebaut – mit klarer Account-Strategie und nachhaltigem Pipeline-Aufbau. 

  • Du interessierst dich für KI im Unternehmenskontext  und kannst Kunden den Unterschied zwischen Hype und echtem Mehrwert erklären. 


Was wir dir bieten

  • Remote-First. Du arbeitest von zuhause oder in unseren Offices in München und Berlin - regelmäßige Team-Events bringen uns offline zusammen. 

  • Onboarding und Ramp-Up, das zu einem komplexen Produkt passt. Produkt, Branche und Methodik step by step - mit erfahrenen Teamkollegen, die dich auf Tempo bringen. 

  • Ehrliches Coaching, präsenter Sales Manager. Wir sind 7 Leute im DACH-Sales, keine Nummer in einer großen Maschine. Regelmäßige Einzelgespräche, gemeinsame Deal-Reviews. Wenn du gut bist, wird das gesehen. Wenn etwas hakt, wird darüber gesprochen. 

  • Karriereperspektive in einer Wachstumsregion. Senior AE, Enterprise AE, Team Lead DACH: wir bauen die Region aktiv aus, nicht ab. 

  • Internationales Setup, lokaler Fokus. Dein Spielfeld ist DACH, aber wenn dich die Lust auf Mailand, Madrid oder Mexico City packt, kannst du auch von dort arbeiten. 

  • 30 Tage Urlaub, Zulage für Heimarbeit und weitere Vorteile folgen in Kürze! 


Dein Weg zu uns

  1. Erstgespräch mit dem Recruiting-Team (30 Min, auf Englisch) – wir lernen uns kennen, klären gegenseitige Erwartungen. 

  1. Interview mit dem Sales Manager DACH (45 Min) – Deep Dive in deine Erfahrung, deine Methodik und Fit für die Rolle. 

  1. Interview mit dem Global Chief Sales Officer (45 Min) – Strategie, Karriereperspektive, Final-Check. 

  1. Kurzes Rollenspiel (45 Min) – eine realistische Sales-Situation, an der wir sehen, wie du arbeitest. Du bekommst Briefing und Vorbereitungszeit. 

Bist du bereit, bei uns einzusteigen?

Schick uns einfach deinen Lebenslauf – wenn möglich auf Englisch – ein Anschreiben ist nicht erforderlich. Wenn du vorab Fragen hast: ----- oder sende eine LinkedIn-Nachricht an Fabian Pohl.

Wir freuen uns über Bewerbungen von allen, unabhängig von Geschlecht, Alter, Herkunft, Religion, sexueller Identität oder Behinderung.

Hinweis: Wir nutzen KI-gestützte Tools zur Vorauswahl von Bewerbungen. Die endgültige Entscheidung trifft immer ein Mensch.

title: Senior DevOps Engineer (all genders)
description:
Sunday Natural is one of Germany’s fastest-growing natural health brands, and our eCommerce platform is growing with it – today it serves 7 million monthly active users, runs on €400k of AWS per year, and supports a development organization of 30+ engineers. Every one of those numbers has moved sharply upward in the last few years, and all of them will keep moving.

You would be our first dedicated in-house Senior DevOps Engineer – and the two biggest engineering projects of the next two years are yours to help define and drive: bringing our entire infrastructure under Terraform, and strengthening the scalability, security and compliance posture across our cloud environments.

Your role

  • You shape the infrastructure vision. How we run, deploy, monitor and scale is yours to define, propose and defend.

  • You work alongside our two external partners as the in-house technical counterpart – building the architecture and standards together, and bringing the deep platform knowledge back into the company. As the platform grows, taking the technical direction of that group is a natural next step, and one we would actively support.

  • You own our AWS spend – €400k a year that currently has no dedicated owner, including where it goes and how we bring it down.

  • You are the escalation point. When production is at risk, you decide.

  • You report directly to the Head of eCommerce Platforms, with direct access to leadership for the decisions that need it.

What you'll own

  • AWS infrastructure – EC2, RDS, Fargate, CloudFront, S3, IAM – plus Cloudflare, DNS and WAF

  • Security & compliance – DevSecOps practices, system audits, patching and access reviews, and GDPR-compliant data handling across every environment

  • Infrastructure as code – taking us from manually managed to fully Terraform-defined

  • Data layer – MySQL under production load: tuning, replication, and backups you have actually restored from

  • Cloud economics – a €350k annual AWS budget with real headroom for optimisation

  • Delivery for 30+ developers – Bitbucket Pipelines, environments, and how fast and safely code reaches production

  • Reliability at 7M MAU – monitoring, logging, alerting and incident response (New Relic, Sentry, CloudWatch, PagerDuty)

Your profile

title: Senior Treasury Manager (m/w/d)
description:
Stellenbeschreibung

Du steuerst Liquidität, Cashflow und Finanzierung in einem Unternehmen mit hoher Dynamik.

Pammys ist in nur vier Jahren auf über 1 Million Kundinnen und Kunden gewachsen und gehört zu den am schnellsten wachsenden E-Commerce-Unternehmen Europas.

Heute arbeiten über 150 Mitarbeitende an unseren Standorten in Hamburg, Kiel und unserem eigenen 22.000 m² Logistikzentrum in Lensahn daran, Pammys zu einer globalen Footwear Brand zu entwickeln.

Mit steigenden Einkaufsvolumina, internationalem Wachstum und hohen Waren- und Marketinginvestitionen wird professionelles Treasury für uns immer wichtiger.

Deshalb suchen wir einen Senior Treasury Manager (m/w/d), der unsere Liquidität vorausschauend steuert, Cashflow-Strukturen optimiert und dafür sorgt, dass unser Wachstum jederzeit solide finanziert ist.


Deine Aufgaben

  • Du verantwortest unsere Liquiditätsplanung und Cashflow-Steuerung und entwickelst rollierende Forecasts für kurz-, mittel- und langfristige Finanzbedarfe.
  • Du steuerst unser Working Capital und optimierst gemeinsam mit Accounting, Controlling, Sourcing und Operations Zahlungsziele, Bestände und Kapitalbindung.
  • Du verantwortest die Zusammenarbeit mit Banken, Finanzierungspartnern und Zahlungsdienstleistern und entwickelst bestehende Finanzierungsstrukturen weiter.
  • Du analysierst finanzielle Risiken und sorgst für ein professionelles Management von Währungs-, Zins- und Liquiditätsrisiken.

Dein Profil

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung im Treasury, Corporate Finance, Cash Management oder Working Capital Management
  • Sehr gutes Verständnis von Liquiditätsplanung, Cashflow, Finanzierung und finanziellen Risiken
  • Erfahrung in einem E-Commerce-, Handels-, Consumer- oder schnell wachsenden Unternehmensumfeld ist ein großes Plus
  • Sicherer Umgang mit Excel sowie Treasury-, ERP- oder Banking-Systemen
  • Erfahrung in der Zusammenarbeit mit Banken und Finanzierungspartnern
  • Du arbeitest analytisch, vorausschauend und präzise und kannst komplexe Finanzthemen klar auf den Punkt bringen


Deine Vorteile bei Pammys

  • Hoher Einfluss: Du steuerst einen der wichtigsten Faktoren unseres weiteren Wachstums: unsere Liquidität.

title: Head of Product Development & Engineering (m/w/d)
description:
Stellenbeschreibung

Wir machen wenige Modelle in großen Stückzahlen — jeder Millimeter am Leisten, im Fußbett und in der Konstruktion multipliziert sich hunderttausendfach. Aus diesem Grund muss der Schuh perfekt sitzen. Du baust Produkte nach der Pammys Bibel. Bisher entwickeln wir eng mit Partnern. Deine Aufgaben

  • Du verantwortest den kompletten Entwicklungsprozess: Brief → Tech-Pack → Proto-Runden → Sales Samples → Sealed Sample → Serienanlauf (Tooling-Trials, PPS, TOP). Jedes technische Gate auf diesem Weg liegt bei dir — inklusive der Freigabe, mit der ein Modell in Serie geht.
  • Du baust dein Team auf und führst es: Footwear Development, Leisten & Passform (Last & Fit), Tooling, Commercialisation und Materials — in der Reihenfolge, die das Wachstum verlangt.
  • Du etablierst Leisten und Passform als Kernkompetenz: eigene Leisten-Bibliothek, Passform-Standards, Grading — bei Comfort-Schuhen ist der Leisten das Produkt.
  • Du entwickelst unsere eigenen Komfort-Technologien für Fußbett und Sohle — gemeinsam mit starken Material- und Compound-Partnern.
  • Du verankerst Wear-Tests sowie Prüf- und Compliance-Standards (SATRA/ISO, REACH, Produktsicherheit für den EU-Markt) im Entwicklungsprozess.
  • Du arbeitest im festen Dreier-Team mit Produktmanagement und Design: Du machst Entwürfe baubar, ohne sie kleinzumachen.

  • Verhandlungssicheres Englisch und Reisebereitschaft.


Deine Vorteile bei Pammys

  • Du baust die technische Produktentwicklung von Grund auf auf: Statt bestehende Strukturen nur zu verwalten, definierst du unsere Standards für Leisten, Passform, Komfort, Tooling und Commercialisation selbst.
  • Echter Einfluss auf das Produkt: Deine Entscheidungen bestimmen unmittelbar, wie unsere Schuhe sitzen, funktionieren und sich im Alltag anfühlen.
  • Große Stückzahlen, große Wirkung: Wir entwickeln bewusst wenige Modelle mit hohem Volumen. Technische Verbesserungen, die du entwickelst, wirken sich direkt auf hunderttausende Produkte aus.

  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit Product, Design und Sourcing: Kurze Wege, schnelle Entscheidungen und keine langen Konzernschleifen zwischen Entwicklung, Design und Produktion.
  • Nähe zu den Foundern: Du arbeitest eng mit den Entscheidungsträgern zusammen und kannst technische Produktentscheidungen direkt auf höchster Ebene beeinflussen.

  • Hoher Qualitätsanspruch statt schneller Kompromisse: Bei Pammys ist Passform kein Detail. Du bekommst den Raum, Standards aufzubauen, mit denen unsere Produkte technisch und qualitativ langfristig besser werden.

title: Analyst Early Stage Team
description:
Analyst Early Stage Investment Team (m/f/d) - Berlin, Munich, London

HV Capital is one of Europe's largest generalist VCs. We invest from pre-seed through growth, across SaaS, fintech, deep tech, and beyond. This is a seat inside the investment team, working directly with partners on sourcing, diligence, and portfolio support.

What you'll actually work on

Finding the next companies before anyone else does. Building market maps in sectors we're excited about, sourcing directly instead of waiting for inbound, running comps, and going deep enough on a space that you know it better than the partner sitting next to you.

Running real diligence. Talking to founders, customers, and competitors. Building the model, not just filling in someone else's template. Stress-testing a business case instead of taking the deck at face value. Writing memos that make a case a partner would actually defend in an investment committee.

Forming your own view, and holding it. We're still making bets on people as much as products, and that means judgment: reading a founder, reading a room, deciding whether you'd trust this person with your own money. That's a muscle, not a checklist.

Sitting in the room, eventually. Partner meetings and deal reviews once you've earned it; not to run them, but to watch how a real investment decision actually gets made, and to have a sharp, well-formed view ready when someone asks for yours.

Portfolio support. The odd KPI request, board-prep question, or research ask from a founder who needs a sharp answer fast, not a polished deck in two weeks.

What good looks like here

We evaluate analysts on judgment and reasoning (can you form an independent view and defend it under pushback), commercial acumen (do you actually understand what makes a business work), deal execution (can you run a process end to end from sourcing, modeling, diligence to closing support), and how you show up in the room. Ownership and curiosity matter as much as any of that. Chasing a thread nobody assigned you, following through without being asked twice.

The craft still matters. A clean model, a memo that holds up, a process run properly. That's the baseline, not optional. What increasingly separates a good analyst from a great one on top of that is judgment: forming a view nobody handed you, and holding it under pushback.

What we're looking for

At least 2 -3 years of real work experience. Beyond that, we don't have one template. We've hired from strategy consulting, banking, asset management, the sciences, and straight out of operating roles at startups. What matters more than your last job title: can you form a view and defend it, can you read a room, do you have an actual edge instead of a template CV?

About PERGOLUX

PERGOLUX is building a category-defining outdoor-living brand—online and now in physical retail. We move fast, test ideas in the real world and give ambitious people room to shape what comes next.

The Opportunity

PERGOLUX is at the starting line of a major new phase of commercial expansion: building a Germany-wide showroom network and the model that can scale beyond it.

This is a chance to join while the playbook is still blank. Working close to leadership, you will help answer where we expand, how we evaluate opportunities, which economics matter and what systems will make the model repeatable.

This is not a pure strategy role. You will call people, chase answers, test live opportunities and build working tools. But your real output is the blueprint—not simply executing a rollout manual, but helping write it.

What You’ll Build

Find the expansion logic

  • Map priority markets, customer demand, retail formats and competitive dynamics.

  • Speak with brokers, landlords, operators and internal teams to test assumptions and close information gaps.

  • Use live location opportunities to learn which criteria truly predict a great showroom.

Build the commercial model

  • Create business cases and scenarios around rent, investment, revenue potential and payback.

  • Define practical scorecards, decision gates and evidence standards for location choices.

  • Turn incomplete data into clear recommendations and commercial trade-offs.

Design the expansion operating system

  • Shape the pipeline, workflows, handovers and information structure behind future expansion.

  • Build lightweight dashboards, automations, templates and AI-enabled tools that remove repetitive work.

  • Identify what should be standardised across markets—and what should stay flexible.

Write the playbook from the first showrooms

  • Compare early assumptions with actual results and customer feedback.

  • Capture what worked, what failed and what should change before the next wave.

  • Turn those lessons into a scalable roadmap and clear guidance for future execution teams.

Your Business Impact

  • Give PERGOLUX a clear answer to where, when and under what conditions physical retail should scale.

  • Make location decisions faster, more consistent and grounded in economics rather than intuition.

  • Create a repeatable expansion playbook that lowers risk and management effort for every new showroom.

What You’ll Bring

  • You are enrolled in or recently graduated from university; your field matters less than how you think and execute.

  • You are a sharp, curious generalist who enjoys moving between research, conversations, numbers and building.

  • You get energy from messy problems, create structure quickly and do not wait for a perfect brief.

title: Cloud Security Engineer
description:
YGO.ai is a VC-funded AI tourism platform. We are hiring a Cloud Security Engineer to own the security of our cloud platform, the APIs our enterprise clients run on and the company itself.


🛡️ About this role. The role carries two things at once. You own security engineering directly and hands-on. You build the security function around it as we grow. At YGO a pod lead is a squad leader and a spokesperson, close to the work and close to the client, rather than a full-time manager. You will not stop being an engineer.

The work is broad. You might review source code in the morning, investigate an endpoint alert after lunch and help design a new authentication flow the next day. You identify the highest-risk problems, decide what happens first and execute.

We serve major travel enterprises and we have enterprise commitments going live from the start of 2027. Security is a condition of that business, not a layer added afterwards.

🧑‍💻 What you'll own

  • Application security. Hands-on code and architecture review across our APIs, backend services and internal tooling. Targeted penetration testing to validate issues yourself. Working with engineers on root causes and practical fixes rather than handing over reports. Vulnerability management and the external penetration tests we commission

  • Detection and response. Knowing we are under attack while it is happening and what happens next. Alerting, intrusion detection, incident process and the on-call path

  • Cloud and platform hardening. Access control, network boundaries, secrets management, containers and the deployment pipeline. Security through the SDLC: CI/CD, repositories and dependencies

  • The security of our APIs. Authentication and authorization, tenant isolation, token scoping and lifecycle, abuse prevention, enterprise SSO and the audit trail our clients and our own accountability depend on

  • The security of our AI systems. Prompt injection, tool and agent permissions, our MCP server, retrieval and data ingestion. The data-residency rules we are held to contractually

  • Identity and company security. SSO, MFA and privileged access for employees, onboarding and offboarding, access reviews, MDM, endpoint security and SaaS access. The practical IT security a company our size needs done, not discussed

  • Secure design across the pods. Threat modelling and design review that enables engineers rather than gatekeeping them and raises the standard of what they ship

  • The security function itself. Set the priorities and the roadmap from actual risk, not security theatre. Decide what we build, buy, automate or leave for later. Grow the team and hire into it, represent security to enterprise clients and carry our SOC 2 programme on Drata. Compliance is part of the job and it is not the centre of it

🚢 What you'll secure

  • An AI search and recommendation engine for major travel enterprises: enterprise integration, SSO, client security reviews, GDS integrations

  • A content enrichment API sold as SaaS: high scale, public facing, data and AI heavy

  • The platform underneath: a client console with organisations, projects and API tokens, supplier and business-client integrations, data ingestion, an MCP server, and several LLM providers behind a single internal library

📚 Our stack

  • Backend: Go monorepo (no framework, 3+ services)

  • Data: PostgreSQL, Redis, Redis Asynq queue

  • Hosting: PaaS-managed containers, Cloudflare in front

  • Observability: Jaeger tracing, BetterStack for logging, alerting and on-call

  • Compliance: Drata, SOC 2 in progress

  • AI tooling: Claude Code, used across the whole team

✅ You must have

  • 5+ years of hands-on security work spanning more than one discipline. Not five years of engineering with some security in it. This role sets the standard for the company, so it needs someone who has seen enough to have judgement rather than opinions

  • Application security depth. You know how modern web applications and APIs are attacked. You can validate an issue yourself through code review or a targeted penetration test and work with the engineer on the fix

  • A strong grasp of authentication and authorization. OAuth and OIDC, sessions, token handling, access control and the failure modes behind most API breaches

  • Cloud security fundamentals, properly. Identity, network, workload and pipeline security on a modern cloud platform, applied to production systems you were responsible for

  • Defensive experience alongside the offensive. You have investigated real incidents. You have built or improved the detection and alerting that catches them

  • Threat modelling and secure architecture for cloud, container and API systems

  • An engineering background. You are comfortable in a codebase, you can review what our engineers and our AI tools produce and you can build what you need yourself. Our backend is Go. Prior Go experience is a plus and not a requirement

  • Comfort in resource-constrained environments. Startups, small security teams or consultancies taught you to prioritize on risk, business impact and available resources and to execute yourself

  • The appetite to build a team. You want to grow this function and eventually lead it. Prior leadership experience is a plus and not a requirement. We would rather have depth and develop the leadership than the reverse

  • Working proficiency with Claude Code. Share specific examples

  • Judgement about pace. You secure a company that ships daily without becoming the reason it stops. Guardrails over gates

  • Experience of SOC 2, ISO 27001 or demanding enterprise security reviews

  • Excellent spoken and written English. You will talk to auditors, client security teams and our own engineers, often in the same week

  • ⚠️ European or African time zones (±3 hours from CET)

  • Available full-time (40 hours per week)

🌟 Nice to have

  • AI and LLM security: prompt injection, agent and tool permissions, model security, retrieval pipelines. Very few security roles let you both use AI as your main tool and secure it as your subject. This one does

  • Early security hire experience. You have been the first or one of the first security hires at a startup or scale-up

  • Experience leading or mentoring security engineers

  • Go

  • Security tooling or automation you built yourself

  • MDM, endpoint protection and identity provider administration (Google Workspace or similar)

  • Compliance automation tooling (Drata, Vanta, Secureframe or similar)

  • Security certifications. Valued as a signal, never required

  • GDPR depth. Travel or GDS exposure

  • German

❤️ You are a great fit if you

  • See security as an engineering discipline. You ship fixes and guardrails, not slide decks

  • Can explain a vulnerability to an engineer and its business risk to a client's security lead in the same afternoon

  • Have done offensive work as a penetration tester or consultant and wanted broader ownership than producing reports

  • Want to build something and own it, rather than advise on someone else's

  • Are comfortable challenging unnecessary security bureaucracy and genuinely risky engineering decisions alike

  • Get frustrated when a security fix takes weeks instead of days

Diese Position ist Teil des Business Intelligence Teams und kann vor Ort, hybrid oder vollständig remote innerhalb Deutschlands besetzt werden. Dein Arbeitsort wird im Voraus vereinbart und bildet die Grundlage deines Arbeitsvertrags.


  • KPI Ownership: Du verantwortest die technischen Definitionen und die zugrunde liegende Logik unserer geschäftskritischen KPIs – allen voran ARR und Umsatz. Dabei geht es nicht nur darum, bestehende Definitionen zu pflegen. Du beurteilst, wann eine technische Definition angepasst werden muss, steuerst Änderungen durch unsere Governance- und Freigabeprozesse, setzt sie technisch um und stehst hinter dem Ergebnis – auch dann, wenn es im Rahmen eines Audits oder durch externe Stakeholder kritisch hinterfragt wird. Dazu gehört auch die Kommunikation: Du erklärst Definitionen und Änderungen proaktiv und verständlich – von operativen Teams bis hin zum Management.

  • Technische Expertise und unsere Datenlandschaft: Du entwickelst, debuggst und prüfst deine eigene analytische Logik. Deine fundierten SQL-Kenntnisse ermöglichen es dir, die benötigten Daten selbst zusammenzustellen, anstatt darauf warten zu müssen, dass andere sie bereitstellen. Du hast ein echtes End-to-End-Verständnis davon, wie Daten aus den Quellsystemen über das Data Warehouse bis ins Reporting gelangen. Dadurch kannst du unterscheiden, ob die Ursache eines Problems in den Daten, im Prozess oder in der Definition liegt. Du erkennst, wann ein Problem an der Quelle behoben werden muss, anstatt es lediglich im Reporting zu korrigieren. Gleichzeitig kannst du einen umfangreichen, laufenden Backlog eigenständig priorisieren und vom ersten Tag an selbstständig bearbeiten, ohne engmaschige Steuerung zu benötigen. Für unsere Pipelines oder die Plattform selbst bist du nicht verantwortlich – das übernehmen unsere Data Engineers, mit denen du eng zusammenarbeitest.

  • Enabling statt reiner Umsetzung: Du gestaltest Definitionen, Modelle und Reportings so, dass Stakeholder ihre weiterführenden Fragen selbst beantworten können, statt für jede einzelne Frage erneut auf BI angewiesen zu sein. Für Finance bedeutet das konkret: Du entwickelst die Datenbasis, Tools und Transparenz, die es dem Team ermöglichen, Themen vollständig selbst zu verantworten, die fachlich bei Finance liegen – beispielsweise den Monatsabschluss oder ARR-Korrekturen. BI verantwortet die Definition und die technische Umsetzung; Finance verantwortet den Prozess und die Kennzahl. Das Ziel ist ein Prozess, den Finance eigenständig durchführen kann.

  • Governance als Change Management: Gemeinsam mit dem Head of BI etablierst und verankerst du ein Governance-Framework für unsere geschäftskritischen KPIs. Ihr definiert, was Ownership auf Business- und BI-Seite konkret bedeutet, wie Definitionen dokumentiert, aktuell und audit-ready gehalten werden und wie Änderungen geprüft, entschieden und kommuniziert werden. Die eigentliche Herausforderung liegt dabei nicht in der Dokumentation, sondern in der Akzeptanz und Anwendung im Unternehmen. Du erhältst sowohl das Mandat als auch die Unterstützung des Leadership-Teams, um diese Veränderung voranzutreiben.

  • Wissenstransfer: Du teilst Workflows, Logiken und Arbeitsweisen mit dem Team. So stellst du sicher, dass die von dir etablierten Standards nicht nur bei dir liegen, sondern nachhaltig im gesamten Team verankert werden.

Das bringst du mit:

  • Du verfügst über mehrere Jahre Berufserfahrung im Bereich Business Intelligence oder Data Analytics. Dabei hast du Themen bereits eigenständig von Anfang bis Ende verantwortet, anstatt lediglich nach vorgegebenen Anforderungen zu arbeiten.

  • SQL ist ein zentraler Bestandteil dieser Rolle und kein Nice-to-have. Du bist sicher darin, komplexe Logiken innerhalb eines mehrschichtigen Data Warehouses zu lesen, zu schreiben und zu debuggen. Dabei denkst du in Datenmodellen und übergreifenden Zusammenhängen, anstatt dich ausschließlich auf einzelne Queries zu konzentrieren.

  • Du verfügst über fundierte Erfahrung mit einem modernen BI-Tool. Wir arbeiten derzeit mit MS Power BI, weshalb Erfahrung mit Power BI besonders wertvoll ist.

  • Du hast Erfahrung mit Business- oder Finanz-KPIs und bist bereit, dich intensiv mit deren Definition und Berechnungslogik auseinanderzusetzen. Kenntnisse von SaaS-Kennzahlen wie ARR und NRR oder von Revenue Recognition sind ein großes Plus. Falls diese Themen für dich noch neu sind, erwarten wir echtes Interesse und die Bereitschaft, dich intensiv einzuarbeiten.

  • Du hast Erfahrung in der engen Zusammenarbeit mit Finance oder anderen Business-Stakeholdern. Du kannst Änderungen an Methoden und Berechnungslogiken auch nicht-technischen Kolleg:innen verständlich erklären und bist gleichzeitig in der Lage, deinen Ansatz zu diskutieren und fundiert zu vertreten, wenn er kritisch hinterfragt wird.

  • Du arbeitest strukturiert, organisierst dich sehr selbstständig und bringst ein hohes Maß an Eigeninitiative mit. Gleichzeitig hast du das nötige Selbstbewusstsein, Ergebnisse zu hinterfragen und klar anzusprechen, wenn du der Meinung bist, dass eine Zahl nicht korrekt ist.

  • Du verfügst über sehr gute Englischkenntnisse auf C1-Niveau. Deutschkenntnisse sind ein Plus.

Nice to have

  • Du hast Erfahrung mit dbt oder einem vergleichbaren Transformation Framework sowie mit versionskontrollierter Analytics-Arbeit. Wir bauen diese Arbeitsweisen aktuell weiter aus, weshalb entsprechende Erfahrung für uns besonders wertvoll ist.

  • Du hast bereits in einem SaaS- oder E-Commerce-Umfeld gearbeitet und kennst die typischen Datenstrukturen und Business-Fragestellungen, die mit diesen Geschäftsmodellen verbunden sind.

  • Du hast praktische Erfahrung mit Data Governance, Datenkatalogen oder der Dokumentation von KPIs. Dir ist bewusst, wie wichtig es ist, Definitionen und Verantwortlichkeiten für Daten im gesamten Unternehmen klar, nachvollziehbar und zugänglich zu machen.

  • Du hattest bereits Berührungspunkte mit Controlling-Themen, Due-Diligence-Prozessen, Audits oder Anforderungen aus dem Investor Reporting. Du verstehst, dass diese Bereiche eine verlässliche Datenbasis, konsistente Definitionen und ein hohes Maß an Genauigkeit erfordern.

title: Working Student Export Control & Trade Compliance (all genders)
description:
About Us

STARK is a new kind of defence technology company. We design, develop, and manufacture high-performance unmanned systems that are software-defined, mass-scalable, and cost-effective, changing how autonomous systems are deployed across multiple domains. This gives our operators a decisive edge in highly contested environments. As threats rise, STARK is strengthening the technological edge of NATO Allies and their Partners to deter aggression and defend Europe.


About the team

Du wirst Teil unseres Teams an der Schnittstelle zwischen internationalem Handel, Exportkontrolle und dem operativen Tagesgeschäft bei STARK. Dabei arbeitest du eng mit Kolleginnen und Kollegen aus verschiedenen Bereichen wie Vertrieb, Einkauf und Logistik zusammen. Von Anfang an arbeitest du an realen Fällen und sammelst praktische Erfahrung in einem schnelllebigen internationalen Umfeld.


Your mission

Als Werkstudent im Bereich Exportkontrolle unterstützt du uns dabei, nationale und internationale Exportkontrollvorgaben zuverlässig in unsere täglichen Geschäftsprozesse zu integrieren.

Du arbeitest eng mit verschiedenen Fachabteilungen wie Vertrieb, Einkauf und Logistik zusammen und unterstützt bei konkreten Fragestellungen rund um Exportgenehmigungen, Sanktionen, Güterklassifizierungen und länderbezogene Restriktionen.

Dabei erhältst du direkten Einblick in reale Fälle des internationalen Handels- und Exportkontrollrechts und kannst dein theoretisches Wissen unmittelbar in der Praxis anwenden.


Responsibilities

  • Du beantwortest tägliche Fragen aus Fachabteilungen, zum Beispiel Vertrieb, Einkauf und Logistik, zu exportkontrollrelevanten Abläufen und Prüfschritten.
  • Du unterstützt aktiv bei der Vorbereitung und Ausarbeitung von Ausfuhrgenehmigungsanträgen beim Bundesamt für Wirtschaft und Ausfuhrkontrolle (BAFA).
  • Vor geplanten Exporten führst du Recherchen zu Exportgenehmigungen, Sanktionen, Güterklassifizierungen und länderbezogenen Restriktionen durch.
  • Du analysierst und dokumentierst vergangene Ausfuhr- und Zolldaten zur Risikoanalyse und zur Vorbereitung interner und externer Audits.
  • Du erstellst, prüfst und verwaltest eigenverantwortlich Endverbleibserklärungen für Kunden, Lieferanten und Behörden.


Qualifications

  • Du bist immatrikulierter Student (all genders) im Bereich Wirtschaftsrecht, Rechtswissenschaften, BWL, Logistik, International Business oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung.
  • Du verfügst über ein grundlegendes Verständnis oder starkes Interesse am deutschen und europäischen Exportkontrollrecht, insbesondere AWG/AWV und der EU-Dual-Use-Verordnung.
  • Du hast Freude daran, komplexe Regelungen verständlich zu vermitteln und deine Kolleginnen und Kollegen lösungsorientiert zu unterstützen.
  • Du arbeitest sehr sorgfältig, strukturiert und eigenverantwortlich.
  • Du verfügst über verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse und sehr gute Englischkenntnisse.


Nice to have

title: Senior Manager - Incentives
description:
This role sits within the Onboarding & Incentives pillar of the Rider Growth function at Deliveroo, this pillar owns the journey from the moment an applicant expresses interest through to a fully habituated, retained rider. We collaborate closely with Product, Data Science, Regional Operations, Rider Marketing and the Retention team to secure and retain a high-quality fleet.

We are seeking a Senior Manager to own three of the core engines behind our rider supply strategy: incentives, performance tracking, and target setting with scope to own wider areas of responsibility as these solutions are productionised.

  1. You will have overall accountability of our rider referral program from strategy to execution. You’ll partner closely with the Retention & Resurrection team on retention incentives, ensuring incentive spend across the rider lifecycle is efficient, well-targeted, and joined up. As part of this, you’ll design the governance frameworks needed to ensure all incentives across referrals, retention, resurrection and activation are operating efficiently and tests are designed robustly.

  2. You will also own performance tracking of rider hours end-to-end, partnering with teams across acquisition, conversion, activation, and retention to understand the forecast and actuals behind their initiatives, and working with Data Science to attribute causality to that work – giving senior stakeholders an accurate, defensible read on how our supply investments are performing.

  3. Finally, you will own our rider applicant target-setting model which is used to determine our rider acquisition forecasts vs top-down targets, working with Science and local Regional Operations teams. Improvements here will ensure we’re able to plan for longer time horizons with greater degrees of accuracy as well as scenario planning with our Rider Marketing team to drive efficiencies in cost per applicant.

What we’re looking for

  • Analytical Rigor: You are highly comfortable building and defending forecasting, target-setting, and attribution models, and can translate complex data into clear, actionable recommendations.

  • Ownership & Follow-Through: You take full accountability for the incentives and reporting you own, proactively flagging risks to plan and driving fixes end-to-end.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: You work effectively across Data Science, Regional Operations, Retention & Resurrection, and Rider Marketing to align on shared goals and targets.

  • Stakeholder Communication: You can distil complex performance and target-setting narratives into clear, credible updates for senior stakeholders.

  • Rider Hours Performance Tracking: Own tracking of rider hours performance, partnering with teams across acquisition, conversion, activation, and retention to understand the forecast and actuals behind their initiatives.

  • Causal Attribution: Partner with Data Science to attribute causality to individual initiatives’ contribution to rider hours, building a robust and defensible measurement framework.

  • Senior Stakeholder Reporting: Ensure rider hours performance and initiative impact are reported accurately and clearly to senior stakeholders on a regular cadence.

  • Weekly Applicant Target Setting: Own the weekly rider applicant target-setting process, ensuring targets reflect the latest view of demand, funnel performance, and onboarding capacity.

  • Annual Planning: Lead applicant target setting within the annual planning cycle, working with Science and local Regional Operations teams to work back from onboard targets to applicant targets.

  • Scenario Planning & Cost Efficiency: Run scenario planning with the Rider Marketing team to stress-test target and budget assumptions and identify opportunities to drive down cost per applicant.

  • Cross-Functional Partnership: Build strong working relationships across Science, Regional Operations, Retention & Resurrection, and Rider Marketing to keep incentive, performance, and target-setting decisions aligned.

Requirements

  • Experience in Operations, Strategy & Operations, or Growth/Performance Marketing, ideally within a high-growth marketplace or on-demand business.

title: Strategy & Operations Manager, Subscription Value Prop & New Benefits
description:
About the team

The Value Proposition & New Benefits team owns what our core value proposition for subscription should be, and the new benefits that bring it to life. We sit within the wider Subscription EMEA org, whose vision is to create the world's leading membership programme in local commerce, delivering unprecedented value and a world-class experience to members.

About the role

We're looking for a Strategy & Operations Manager to own strategy and execution for new benefits within Subscription. This is a hybrid strategy/build/run role: you'll define what to launch, then work cross-functionally to get it shipped and measure whether it's working. You'll be expected to move fluidly between strategic thinking and hands-on execution - this is not a role where strategy stops at a slide deck.

Typical problems you'll solve:

  • What new benefits should we launch for Subscription - which ideas are worth pursuing, and what's the business case for each?

  • How do we prioritise and sequence a pipeline of benefit ideas against limited engineering, design, and operational capacity?

  • How do we define success for a new benefit before launch - what does a good outcome look like, and what would tell us to kill it?

  • Once live, how is a benefit actually performing - impact on acquisition, retention, frequency, and member satisfaction - against its cost to serve, and what does that tell us to do next?

  • How do we take a benefit from a small pilot to a scaled, steady-state feature, and what needs to be true operationally for that to work?

What you'll be doing

  • Own the strategy and roadmap for new benefits within Subscription - build the analysis, the business case, and the plan, and drive it through to execution.

  • Cross-functional delivery - partner with Product, Engineering, Design, Data Science, Marketing, and Finance to take benefit ideas from concept to launch, without formal authority over any of them.

  • Build and prioritise the benefit pipeline - evaluate a stream of ideas (experiential, use-case specific, or otherwise), size their potential impact and cost, and decide what's worth building next.

  • Track ongoing performance - maintain visibility into each live benefit's impact on acquisition, retention, frequency, and satisfaction against its cost to serve, flagging when something needs attention.

  • Scale what works - take benefits from small pilots to steady-state features, defining the operating model, reporting cadence, and processes needed to run them sustainably.

  • Bring outside-in perspective - track what Uber One, DashPass, Wolt+, Just Eat and Amazon Prime are doing with membership benefits, and translate what's relevant into Deliveroo's context.

  • Communicate to senior stakeholders - write clear strategy documents and present recommendations, trade-offs, and results to leadership.

Requirements

  • 5+ years of experience in strategy & operations, strategy consulting, or business operations - ideally with exposure to marketplaces, subscription/membership businesses, or consumer tech.

  • Commercial acumen: strong understanding of marketplace dynamics and subscriber value; comfortable building a business case and owning a set of P&L-adjacent metrics.

  • Analytical rigor: comfortable interpreting data and experiment results to make a clear business call - you'll partner with Data Science on the "how" and "so what."

  • Bias for action and ownership: able to bring structure and clarity to ambiguous problems ("what should we build, and how will we know it worked?"), and to drive execution personally rather than just recommend.

  • Cross-functional influence: track record of aligning senior stakeholders and diverse functions (Product, Eng, Finance, Marketing) around a shared plan in a fast-moving, matrixed environment.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication - able to distill complex trade-offs into a clear recommendation for leadership.

Why Deliveroo

Our mission is to transform the way you shop and eat, bringing the neighbourhood to your door by connecting consumers, restaurants, shops and riders. We are transforming the way the world eats and shops by making access to food and products more convenient and enjoyable. We give people the opportunity to buy what they want, as they want it, when and where they want it.

We are a technology-driven company at the forefront of the most rapidly expanding industry in the world. We are still a small team, making a very large impact, looking to answer some of the most interesting questions out there. We move fast, value autonomy and ownership, and we are always looking for new ideas.

Workplace & Benefits

At Deliveroo we know that people are the heart of the business and we prioritise their welfare. Benefits differ by country, but we offer many benefits in areas including healthcare, well-being, parental leave, pensions, and generous annual leave allowances, including time off to support a charitable cause of your choice. Benefits are country-specific, please ask your recruiter for more information.

Diversity

At Deliveroo, we believe a great workplace is one that represents the world we live in and how beautifully diverse it can be. That means we have no judgement when it comes to any one of the things that make you who you are - your gender, race, sexuality, religion or a secret aversion to coriander.   • Design, build, and operate production systems across backend services and user-facing applications.

  • Lead technically complex initiatives across areas such as merchant onboarding, analytics, recommendations, menu and order management, integrations, or merchant-facing tools.

  • Translate ambiguous business and merchant problems into scalable, pragmatic technical solutions.

  • Drive technical design and architecture decisions, considering scalability, reliability, maintainability, and long-term product needs.

Our backend services primarily use Go and Kotlin, while our frontend applications use technologies such as TypeScript and React.

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
Odin is building the investment infrastructure for the future of private markets.
We believe capital is one of the most powerful tools for shaping the world - and more people should know how to put it to work. Our mission is to make it radically easier to raise and deploy capital, so that anyone, anywhere, can back the companies and ideas they believe in.

Our first product is a full-stack platform for launching and running private investment firms - think Shopify for VC and PE. We handle all the infrastructure: from legal structuring and investor onboarding to KYC/AML, payments, tax, reporting, and exits.

We’re already trusted by over 10,000 angels, VCs, and founders. We administer over $500m in assets, covering investments from pre-seed to series E. This includes household names like ElevenLabs, OpenAI, SpaceX, xAI, Anduril, etc. but also new companies creating everything from synthetic brains to small nuclear reactors.

Why we’re hiring

  • We're post-PMF and revenue generating, launching in the US ahead of a Series A. Early enough that you'll shape how engineering works here, late enough that you're not gambling on whether the product works.

  • You'll own significant parts of the product and ship the things customers feel most. It's a regulated platform moving money across multiple jurisdictions, so the work has to be right and it still has to be fast.

  • We also want the bar to move while you're here. Senior engineers set the standard through the quality of what they ship, how they review, and the problems they choose to fix rather than work around.

  • Alongside that, we're rethinking how we build with AI. We use the tools, but we know there's a step change available to teams who redesign their whole workflow around them rather than adding AI to how they already work. If you've already done that somewhere else, you'll have a lot of room here.

What we're looking for

  • You've built and run non-trivial production systems, and you've learned what works in which situations rather than defaulting to one approach.

  • Strong architectural judgement. Most of our code is now written by an LLM, which means you need to own the decisions around it: how the system is structured, what the patterns are, whether the thing being built is the right thing at all. Our stack is Go, and if you learn quickly, not having written it isn't a problem.

  • A serious AI practice. You can talk specifically about how AI has changed the way you build, what it's actually made faster, and what you've shared with the teams you've worked in.

  • Directness. You give feedback when something isn't good enough and take it just as well.

  • Good instincts about what's worth doing. You know when something needs to be built properly and when it doesn't, and you push for the work that makes everyone around you faster.

Probably not for you if

You think the impact of AI on engineering is overstated. You'd rather be handed a fully specified ticket than question the brief. Or the learning curve across finance, compliance and multiple jurisdictions sounds like a chore rather than the interesting part.

The people who do well here find that last bit genuinely interesting. Understanding how capital actually moves, and what the rules allow in each jurisdiction, is most of what makes this product hard to build and hard to copy.

The hiring process

Three stages, usually inside two weeks, with detailed feedback within 24 hours of each one.

  1. Call with Imani, our Head of People and Talent. You'll get a proper picture of the role and the company, and we'll get into how you work and how you build.

  2. System design session with our engineering team. No leetcode and no take-home. We want to see how you approach a problem and structure a solution.

  3. Paid trial day. A real Odin problem with everything you need handed to you. You see how we work, we see how you ship.

Working at Odin

Two setups work for this role: London hybrid (three days a week in the office) or remote from elsewhere in Europe with quarterly trips to London.

  • Parental Leave: Enhanced maternity, adoption, paternity and partner leave
